*Early Life and Inheritance*
Raymond III was born around 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Hodierna of Jerusalem. He inherited the County of Tripoli after his father death in 1152. His mother acted as regent until he reached maturity. He grew up in the Crusader state surrounded by Muslim neighbours and Latin allies. His upbringing emphasized martial training and diplomatic awareness.

*Military and Diplomatic Activities*
Raymond III took an active role in the defence of the County. He participated in the Battle of Hattin in 1187 where the Crusader army suffered a disastrous defeat. After the loss he worked to regroup the remaining forces and to negotiate with Saladin. He also engaged in occasional raids against Muslim territories to protect trade routes. Raymond III maintained contacts with the Kings of Jerusalem and with the Byzantine Empire seeking support. He negotiated truces that allowed the County to survive despite surrounding pressures. His diplomatic skill helped preserve Tripoli for several years after the fall of Jerusalem.

*Death and Legacy*
Raymond III died in 1187 shortly after the Battle of Hattin. Some sources claim he died of wounds others say he died of illness. His son Raymond IV succeeded him but the County faced increasing pressure from Muslim forces. The County of Tripoli eventually fell to the Mamluks in 1289. Raymond III is remembered as a capable leader who tried to balance military action with negotiation. His efforts illustrate the challenges faced by Crusader nobles in the twelfth century.
